newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Redemptions in Israeli provident funds resume.
newsitem.headline: Redemptions in Israeli provident funds resume.

text.p: Net redemptions in Israeli provident funds reached 266 million shekels in January, reversing the brief inflow they enjoyed in December, the Treasury said on Monday.

The provident funds suffered net redemptions of 11.7 billion shekels in 1996, although in December they enjoyed a rare net inflow of 397 million shekels. Savers traditionally put money into the funds at the end of the year for tax reasons.
Provident funds are long-term savings schemes that invest most of their assets in Treasury bonds.

The Treasury said savings programmes also suffered with net withdrawals for January although it was a small 65 million shekels. Inflation-linked programmes experienced a slight increase in deposits while foreign currency-linked deposits saw withdrawals of 84 million shekels.
Savings programmes have been the recipients of deposits in the last two years, taking in a total of 5.36 billion shekels last year alone, the Treasury said.
